claims.summary: For a finite experiment of m likelihoods on a central finite-dimensional tracial algebra of real selfadjoint dimension N, an optimal rank-one canonical measurement exists with at most N+m outcomes; preserving its full channel requires at most N+N(N+1)/2 outcomes.
A bounded-sandwich, selfcompatible dephasing example with zero residual requires at least d outcomes for exact EB reconstruction; approximate error epsilon implies K >= d[1-(4d+1)epsilon].

For block-supported rank-one POVMs, central reference weights cancel from physical preparation, while measurement selection still depends on reference weights and acquired likelihoods; conditional block-weight sampling and precision costs are quantified.
Finite rational experiments admit an in-principle real-algebraic QE synthesis procedure, without a polynomial cost bound; the unrestricted c-Dirichlet or broadcasting-to-EB theorem remains open.
